subtopic_gates.learner_title: Chemical Symbols, Atomic Notation & Formula Literacy

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9 & 10 Science (Chemistry)
provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 9 Science Chapter 3 (Atoms and Molecules), Sections 3.2-3.4

technical_core.canonical_statement: An atom is designated by symbol X with atomic number Z (protons) and mass number A (protons + neutrons) as ^A_Z X.
technical_core.why_required: Grounds element identity and atomic composition.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Conflating isotopes or confusing atomic mass with atomic number.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Elementary gases exist as stable diatomic molecules (H2, N2, O2, F2, Cl2, Br2, I2) under standard conditions.
technical_core.why_required: Prevents writing monoatomic elemental gases in chemical equations.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Writing isolated O or H instead of O2 or H2 as chemical reactants.

technical_core.canonical_statement: A subscript denotes the number of bonded atoms in a formula unit; a stoichiometric coefficient denotes the number of distinct formula units.
technical_core.why_required: Prevents catastrophic confusion between substance identity and substance quantity.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating 2H as equivalent to H2.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: A mass number, Z atomic number, N neutron count
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Non-negative integers

representations.name: Nuclide Symbol Notation
representations.chemistry_encoded: Top-left mass number, bottom-left atomic number, centered chemical symbol
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Superscript mass number and subscript atomic number placement
representations.common_incorrect_version: Writing mass number as right subscript or confusing with charge
representations.verification_method: Check A >= Z and A - Z equals integer neutron count

model_conditions.condition: Non-relativistic atomic nucleus
model_conditions.why_needed: Nucleon conservation holds strictly
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Nuclear transmutation or mass defect occurs

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify element symbol from periodic authority
Extract proton count Z and calculate neutron count N = A - Z
Distinguish between free elemental atoms and stable diatomic molecules

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: 2H is chemically identical to H2
misconceptions.why_plausible: Both contain two hydrogen atoms total
misconceptions.required_counterexample: H2 is stable diatomic gas with covalent bond; 2H represents two separate reactive radical atoms
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce: subscripts modify internal stoichiometry; coefficients scale external quantity

mandatory_verifications: INTEGER_COUNT_CHECK
MASS_CHARGE_CONSERVATION

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Ions, Valency, Polyatomic Radicals & Formal Charge

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9 Science
provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 9 Science Chapter 3, Section 3.4 (What is an Ion?)

technical_core.canonical_statement: An ion is a charged atom or group of atoms formed by the loss of electrons (cation, positive) or gain of electrons (anion, negative).
technical_core.why_required: Establishes physical origin of electrical charge in chemical species.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Believing ions are formed by proton transfer.

technical_core.canonical_statement: A polyatomic ion is a covalently bonded cluster of atoms carrying an overall net charge that acts as a single indivisible chemical unit (e.g. SO4^2-, CO3^2-, NH4+).
technical_core.why_required: Required to prevent decomposing stable radicals during formula writing.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Writing Al2SO43 instead of Al2(SO4)3.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Valency is the combining capacity of an element or radical, corresponding to the number of electrons lost, gained, or shared to achieve a noble gas electron configuration.
technical_core.why_required: Provides predictive capacity for chemical formula construction.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Blind memorization of formulas without valency basis.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: q_ion net charge, Z proton count, N_e electron count, e elementary charge
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Signed integer multiple of e

representations.name: Lewis Charge Bracket Diagram
representations.chemistry_encoded: Element or cluster enclosed in brackets with formal charge indicated as superscript
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit sign and magnitude outside bracket
representations.common_incorrect_version: Writing charge inside brackets or omitting magnitude
representations.verification_method: Check total valence electrons minus formal bonds equals net bracket charge

model_conditions.condition: Integer electron transfer
model_conditions.why_needed: Charge quantization holds strictly
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Fractional charges occur only in subatomic quark theory, invalid in chemistry

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify valence shell electron configuration
Determine electrons gained or lost to satisfy octet/duplet rule
Assign signed ionic charge and deduce combining valency

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Brackets are optional when writing multiple polyatomic ions (e.g. writing CaOH2 or Al2SO43)
misconceptions.why_plausible: Learner treats the radical as ordinary concatenated letters
misconceptions.required_counterexample: CaOH2 means 1 Ca, 1 O, 2 H; calcium hydroxide requires 2 hydroxide ions Ca(OH)2 (1 Ca, 2 O, 2 H)
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce brackets around polyatomic radical whenever subscript is 2 or greater

mandatory_verifications: CHARGE_QUANTIZATION_CHECK
OCTET_SATISFACTION_CHECK

problem_families.name: Ion Charge and Valency Determination
problem_families.recognition_cues: Given atomic number or group number, deduce ion formula and valency
problem_families.first_technical_move: Write electron configuration and determine distance to nearest noble gas
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Assigning positive charge to an atom that gains electrons

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Subatomic charge calculation and polyatomic radical bracket rules

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Omitting parentheses around polyatomic ion with subscript > 1
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Polyatomic radicals require brackets when multiplied by stoichiometric subscripts

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Chemical Formula Construction & Electroneutrality

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9 Science
provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 9 Science Chapter 3, Section 3.4.2 (Writing Chemical Formulae)

technical_core.canonical_statement: In any stable chemical compound, the total positive charge contributed by cations must exactly balance the total negative charge contributed by anions, resulting in net zero charge.
technical_core.why_required: Enforces fundamental physical condition for macroscopic stability.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Tolerating unneutralized ionic formulas such as MgCl or NaSO4.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Chemical formulas are constructed by crossing valencies/charges as opposite subscripts and reducing to simplest integer ratio.
technical_core.why_required: Provides deterministic algorithm for formula generation.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Guessing subscripts or writing unreduced ratios such as Mg2O2.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: n_+ cation count, z_+ cation charge, n_- anion count, z_- anion charge
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Signed integer charge summation

representations.name: Criss-Cross Valency Diagram
representations.chemistry_encoded: Cation and anion symbols at top, numerical valencies beneath, diagonal crossing lines pointing to subscripts
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit crossing vectors and integer simplification step
representations.common_incorrect_version: Carrying the plus/minus signs into the subscripts (e.g. Mg2+ Cl1- -> Mg-Cl2+)
representations.verification_method: Check total cation charge + total anion charge == 0

model_conditions.condition: Simplest empirical formula unit for ionic lattices
model_conditions.why_needed: Ionic compounds form continuous lattices, not discrete molecules
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Writing NaCl as Na2Cl2 or continuous polymers without stoichiometric justification

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Write symbols of constituent ions with cation first
Write valencies or charge magnitudes below each ion
Criss-cross valencies to form provisional subscripts
Divide by greatest common divisor to simplest integer ratio
Enclose polyatomic radicals in brackets if subscript > 1

required_transformations.description: Magnesium oxide -> Mg^2+, O^2- -> Mg2O2 -> MgO

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Elements combine 1:1 regardless of valency (e.g. magnesium chloride is MgCl)
misconceptions.why_plausible: Overgeneralizing binary formulas from NaCl
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Mg loses 2 electrons; each Cl accepts only 1 electron. Therefore 2 Cl ions are required to balance 1 Mg ion: MgCl2
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce net charge electroneutrality check on every proposed formula

mandatory_verifications: CHARGE_NEUTRALITY_CHECK
SIMPLEST_INTEGER_RATIO_CHECK

problem_families.name: Binary and Polyatomic Formula Construction
problem_families.recognition_cues: Given chemical name of salt or constituent ions, formulate neutral chemical formula
problem_families.first_technical_move: Identify ion charges, write criss-cross valencies, and check for radical brackets
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Leaving unreduced subscripts like Mg2O2 or omitting radical brackets

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Electroneutrality constraints and polyatomic bracket rules

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Writing formula that violates electroneutrality
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Total positive charge must equal total negative charge in stable compound

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Conservation of Mass & Chemical Equation Balancing

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 10 Science
provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 1 (Chemical Reactions and Equations), Section 1.1.2

technical_core.canonical_statement: Mass cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction; total mass of reactants must equal total mass of products.
technical_core.why_required: Fundamental governing physical conservation law for chemistry.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating unbalanced equations as physically valid representations.

technical_core.canonical_statement: The number of atoms of each element remains strictly conserved before and after a chemical reaction.
technical_core.why_required: Provides the mathematical basis for stoichiometric balancing.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Chemical equations that create or destroy elemental atoms.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Balancing must be achieved exclusively by adjusting integer stoichiometric coefficients in front of formulas; chemical subscripts are strictly immutable.
technical_core.why_required: Altering subscripts mutates the identity of the chemical substance into a different or non-existent compound.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Balancing H2 + O2 by writing H2O2 instead of 2H2O.

mandatory_equations.formula: sum_reactants nu_i * N_{i, k} = sum_products nu_j * N_{j, k}
mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: nu stoichiometric coefficient, N_{i, k} number of atoms of element k in formula unit i

symbols.name: Atom count of element k in species i

mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Exact element-wise equality

representations.name: Atom Inventory Ledger
representations.chemistry_encoded: Three-column ledger: Element Name, Left Hand Side (Reactant) count, Right Hand Side (Product) count
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit counts for all elements and verification that LHS == RHS
representations.common_incorrect_version: Counting atoms without multiplying through by prefix coefficients
representations.verification_method: Check LHS atom count equals RHS atom count for every element in the table

model_conditions.condition: Ordinary chemical reaction (non-nuclear)
model_conditions.why_needed: Nuclear identities are conserved
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Nuclear transmutation requires mass-energy conservation E=mc^2

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Write skeleton equation with verified correct chemical formulas
Compile atom inventory table for all elements
Select element appearing in fewest formulas (usually metal/nonmetal, leaving H and O last)
Insert trial integer coefficient and immediately update inventory
Balance remaining elements (H then O) and verify all counts match

required_transformations.description: Fe + H2O -> Fe3O4 + H2 balanced to 3Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2
Hydrogen + Chlorine -> Hydrogen chloride balanced to H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Subscripts can be changed to make atoms balance (e.g. H2 + O2 -> H2O2 to form water)
misconceptions.why_plausible: Mechanically equalizes oxygen count quickly
misconceptions.required_counterexample: H2O is water; H2O2 is hydrogen peroxide, a completely different toxic bleaching agent
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Strict prohibition: formula subscripts are immutable; balance only with leading coefficients

mandatory_verifications: ELEMENT_WISE_ATOM_CONSERVATION_CHECK
COEFFICIENT_INTEGER_SIMPLIFICATION_CHECK

problem_families.name: Inspection and Algebraic Equation Balancing
problem_families.recognition_cues: Unbalanced skeleton equation requiring lowest whole number integer coefficients
problem_families.first_technical_move: Construct atom inventory table and identify most complex formula unit to anchor
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Changing subscripts within formula units or using fractional coefficients without clearing
problem_families.typical_unknown: Set of lowest whole-number integer coefficients

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: High element interactivity and multi-step linear dependency across coupled equations

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Balancing an equation by mutating a chemical subscript
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Subscripts define substance identity and are strictly immutable during equation balancing

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Physical State Symbols, Precipitation & Gas Evolution

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 10 Science
provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 1, Section 1.1.2 (Making Equation More Informative)

technical_core.canonical_statement: Every reactant and product in a complete chemical equation must declare its physical state: solid (s), liquid (l), gas (g), or aqueous solution (aq).
technical_core.why_required: Chemical behavior, enthalpy, and reaction pathway depend critically on aggregation state.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating gaseous water (steam) as identical to liquid water.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Liquid (l) denotes a pure liquid substance or solvent; aqueous (aq) denotes a solute dissolved in water, existing as hydrated ions or solvated molecules.
technical_core.why_required: Dissolved ionic compounds behave completely differently from molten or pure liquids.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Writing HCl(l) for hydrochloric acid or NaCl(l) for table salt dissolved in water.

technical_core.canonical_statement: An insoluble solid formed from mixing solutions is a precipitate indicated by (s) or down-arrow; an evolved gas is indicated by (g) or up-arrow.
technical_core.why_required: Ties macroscopic reaction phenomena directly to chemical state.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Failing to recognize precipitate in double displacement reactions.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: BaCl2 aqueous barium chloride, Na2SO4 aqueous sodium sulfate, BaSO4 solid precipitate, NaCl aqueous sodium chloride
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: State symbol suffix on every species

representations.name: State-Annotated Chemical Equation
representations.chemistry_encoded: Balanced equation with explicit subscript/suffix state symbols and directional arrows
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: State notation on every chemical participant
representations.common_incorrect_version: Writing naked formulas without state symbols in aqueous reactions
representations.verification_method: Verify solubility rules to confirm precipitate state is (s)

model_conditions.condition: Aqueous solution at 1 atm and 25 deg C
model_conditions.why_needed: Solubility product criteria apply
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: High temperature or non-aqueous solvent alters solubility

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify solvent and dissolved status of each participant
Apply solubility rules to determine whether product forms precipitate
Append appropriate state symbol suffix to every participant

required_transformations.description: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 -> CaO(s) + H2O(l) -> Ca(OH)2(aq)
White precipitate on mixing lead nitrate and potassium iodide -> PbI2(s)

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Aqueous solution and liquid are interchangeable, so HCl(aq) is the same as HCl(l)
misconceptions.why_plausible: Both appear as fluids in a beaker
misconceptions.required_counterexample: HCl(l) is pure liquefied hydrogen chloride at -85 deg C; HCl(aq) is dissolved H+ and Cl- ions in water exhibiting acidic properties
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Strict distinction: (l) is pure liquid; (aq) is water-solvated solution

mandatory_verifications: SOLUBILITY_PRODUCT_PRECIPITATE_CHECK
STATE_COMPLETENESS_CHECK

problem_families.recognition_cues: Aqueous double displacement reaction with potential insoluble product
problem_families.first_technical_move: Determine cation-anion exchange pairs and check solubility table
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Labeling soluble salt as solid precipitate or leaving off state symbols

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Distinction between pure phases and solvated aqueous species

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Conflating pure liquid with aqueous solution
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Aqueous species must be distinguished from pure liquid phases

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Reaction Conditions, Enthalpy & Catalytic Constraints

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 10 Science
provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 1, Section 1.1.2 & Chapter 2

technical_core.canonical_statement: Reaction arrows declare pathway reversibility: a single forward arrow indicates an irreversible reaction; a double half-arrow indicates dynamic chemical equilibrium.
technical_core.why_required: Distinguishes completion reactions from equilibrium systems.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating reversible Haber process or esterification as one-way completion.

technical_core.canonical_statement: External constraints such as temperature (Delta), pressure, light (h*nu), or specific catalysts must be annotated directly above and below the reaction arrow.
technical_core.why_required: Reactions do not proceed without meeting activation and kinetic thresholds.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Presenting high-barrier industrial syntheses as spontaneous room-temperature reactions.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Exothermic reactions release heat (Delta H < 0, heat on product side); endothermic reactions absorb heat (Delta H > 0, heat on reactant side).
technical_core.why_required: Enforces energy conservation and temperature change predictions.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Conflating heat absorption with heat release in decomposition reactions.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: CO2 carbon dioxide, H2O water, C6H12O6 glucose, O2 oxygen; sunlight and chlorophyll are required catalysts/energy sources
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Catalyst/light annotated across arrow

representations.name: Reaction Coordinate Diagram
representations.chemistry_encoded: Potential energy vs reaction coordinate showing activation energy barrier and Delta H
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Clear relative energy of products vs reactants and catalyst barrier lowering
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing exothermic reaction with products higher than reactants
representations.verification_method: Check Delta H = H_products - H_reactants agrees with sign

model_conditions.condition: Constant pressure thermochemical system
model_conditions.why_needed: Enthalpy Delta H equals heat exchanged
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Non-constant pressure requires internal energy Delta U analysis

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify if activation energy requires external input (heat, light, catalyst)
Place external energy/catalyst annotations directly across reaction arrow
Assign enthalpy sign Delta H based on bond breaking vs bond making

required_transformations.description: Heating limestone to make quicklime -> CaCO3(s) -(Delta)-> CaO(s) + CO2(g)
Energy absorbed -> Decomposition reaction is endothermic (Delta H > 0)

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: If an equation is balanced, the reaction occurs spontaneously at room temperature
misconceptions.why_plausible: Paper chemistry does not display activation energy barriers
misconceptions.required_counterexample: H2 + O2 can sit mixed indefinitely at 25 deg C without reacting; a spark is required to overcome activation energy
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Explicitly mandate reaction condition annotations on every non-spontaneous transformation

mandatory_verifications: ENTHALPY_SIGN_CONSISTENCY_CHECK
CATALYST_INVARIANCE_CHECK

problem_families.name: Reaction Condition and Thermochemical Classification
problem_families.recognition_cues: Reaction with temperature, catalyst, or Delta H indicators
problem_families.first_technical_move: Read arrow annotations and determine if reaction is exothermic or endothermic
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Classifying thermal decomposition as exothermic
problem_families.typical_unknown: Reaction type and required catalytic conditions

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Thermodynamic and kinetic condition requirements across reaction pathways

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Omitting required external conditions on non-spontaneous reactions
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Endothermic or catalytic reactions must declare required external conditions

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Johnstone's Triplet (Particulate <-> Symbolic <-> Macroscopic)
subtopic_gates.chapter: Chemical Reactions and Equations / Chemical Foundations

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9 & 10 Science
provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 1 & Johnstone Chemical Education Framework

technical_core.canonical_statement: Chemical understanding requires coherent translation across three levels: Macroscopic (tangible observations), Sub-microscopic / Particulate (atoms, molecules, ions), and Symbolic (formulas, equations, mathematics).
technical_core.why_required: Prevents rote symbolic formula manipulation disconnected from physical reality.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Learner manipulating equations without any mental model of reacting particles.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Every macroscopic observation (color change, temperature rise, precipitate, effervescence) must be causally linked to specific particulate species transformations.
technical_core.why_required: Ensures scientific causal attribution in chemical explanations.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Vague explanations attributing color change to 'the reaction' rather than specific product species.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Shows direct binding between ionic species, formulas, and macroscopic visible phenomena
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Causal triplet linkage

representations.name: Three-Level Chemistry Triplet Diagram
representations.chemistry_encoded: Three synchronized panels: Beaker photograph/sketch (Macroscopic), Ball-and-stick/particle model (Sub-microscopic), Chemical equation (Symbolic)
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit bidirectional cross-reference links between particles and chemical formulas
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing macroscopic beaker and equation but omitting particulate representation
representations.verification_method: Verify atom count in particulate model strictly matches coefficients in symbolic equation

model_conditions.condition: Discrete particle particulate model
model_conditions.why_needed: Atoms and molecules obey discrete counting
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Continuous fluid mechanics assumptions blur chemical atomicity

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Record concrete macroscopic observation (e.g. effervescence, precipitate)
Map observation to chemical species formed (e.g. gas molecules, insoluble lattice)
Write balanced symbolic equation reflecting particulate transformation

required_transformations.description: Fizzes and bubbles -> Gas molecules dispersing from liquid
Counting 2 diatomic A2 and 1 diatomic B2 in box -> 2A2 + B2 -> 2A2B

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Individual sub-microscopic particles possess macroscopic properties (e.g. a sulfur atom is yellow, an atom of gold expands when heated)
misconceptions.why_plausible: Direct psychological projection of bulk sensory observations onto single atoms
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Color is an optical property of bulk electronic transitions; a single isolated atom has no bulk macroscopic color or melting point
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Strictly distinguish between emergent bulk macroscopic phenomena and single-particle quantum/atomic states

mandatory_verifications: PARTICLE_TO_SYMBOLIC_COUNT_MATCH
OBSERVATION_CAUSAL_TRACE_CHECK

problem_families.name: Particulate-Box to Chemical Equation Translation
problem_families.recognition_cues: Diagram showing reacting particles in closed container before and after reaction
problem_families.first_technical_move: Count reactant molecules, identify excess species, and write stoichiometric ratio
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Including spectator or unreacted molecules as part of the core balanced equation
problem_families.typical_unknown: Balanced symbolic equation and limiting reactant

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Simultaneous coordination across sensory macroscopic, particulate sub-microscopic, and abstract symbolic representations

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Attributing macroscopic bulk properties to individual atoms
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Single atoms do not possess bulk macroscopic sensory properties

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Stoichiometry, Mole Conversions & Limiting Reagents

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9 & 11 Science (Chemistry)
provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 9 Science Chapter 3, Section 3.5 (Mole Concept) & Grade 11 Chapter 1

technical_core.canonical_statement: One mole is the amount of substance containing exactly 6.02214076 x 10^23 elementary entities, with mass in grams numerically equal to relative formula mass.
technical_core.why_required: Connects microscopic particle counts directly to macroscopic weighable grams.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Inability to perform quantitative chemical calculations.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Stoichiometric coefficients define the exact molar ratios in which substances react and form, never direct mass ratios.
technical_core.why_required: Chemical reactions occur atom-for-atom and molecule-for-molecule, not gram-for-gram.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Equating coefficients directly to gram masses.

technical_core.canonical_statement: The limiting reagent is the reactant completely consumed first in a reaction, thereby capping the theoretical maximum yield of all products.
technical_core.why_required: Real reaction mixtures are rarely in exact stoichiometric balance.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Assuming all reactants are completely consumed regardless of initial quantities.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: n moles, m sample mass, M molar mass, N entity count, N_A Avogadro constant
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Non-negative real quantities
mandatory_equations.conditions_of_validity: Pure chemical substance with known molecular formula

representations.name: Before-Change-After (BCA) Mole Table
representations.chemistry_encoded: Structured table tracking moles of all species before reaction, during change (-nu*x, +nu*x), and after completion
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Change line must strictly reflect stoichiometric coefficient ratios
representations.common_incorrect_version: Filling BCA table with gram masses instead of molar quantities
representations.verification_method: Check final moles >= 0 and limiting reagent final moles == 0

model_conditions.condition: 100% reaction completion without side reactions
model_conditions.why_needed: Theoretical yield calculation applies
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Incomplete reaction or equilibrium requires percent yield calculation

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Convert all given reactant masses or particle counts into moles (n = m/M)
Divide each reactant mole quantity by its stoichiometric coefficient to identify limiting reagent
Use limiting reactant moles to compute theoretical yield of products via molar ratio
Convert product moles back to requested units (grams or liters)

required_transformations.description: 2 mol H2 reacting with 1 mol O2 produces 2 mol H2O (36 g)

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Coefficients in an equation represent masses in grams (e.g. 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O means 2g H2 reacts with 1g O2)
misconceptions.why_plausible: Confusing stoichiometric integer count with macroscopic gram weight
misconceptions.required_counterexample: 2 mol H2 has mass 4g; 1 mol O2 has mass 32g; they react in 4g : 32g (1:8 mass ratio), not 2:1
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce mandatory conversion: mass -> moles -> mole ratio -> product mass

mandatory_verifications: LIMITING_REAGENT_NON_NEGATIVE_CHECK
MASS_CONSERVATION_CLOSURE_CHECK

problem_families.first_technical_move: Compute molar mass from periodic table and apply n = m/M
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Using atomic mass instead of molecular mass for diatomic elements

problem_families.name: Limiting Reagent and Theoretical Yield Calculation
problem_families.recognition_cues: Given starting masses of two or more reactants

problem_families.common_fatal_error: Choosing limiting reactant by comparing masses directly without converting to moles
problem_families.typical_unknown: Limiting reactant and mass of product formed

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Multi-step quantitative dimensional analysis and limiting reactant branching logic

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Treating stoichiometric coefficients as gram mass ratios
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Stoichiometric coefficients dictate molar ratios, requiring molar mass conversion

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Acids, Bases, Aqueous Ionization & Net Ionic Neutralization

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 10 Science
provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 2 (Acids, Bases and Salts), Sections 2.1-2.3

technical_core.canonical_statement: Acids produce hydrogen/hydronium ions (H+ / H3O+) and bases produce hydroxide ions (OH-) exclusively in aqueous solution; moisture is mandatory for acidic/basic behavior.
technical_core.why_required: Explains why dry HCl gas or anhydrous citric acid fails to change dry litmus paper.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Believing acids act independently of water or solvent ionization.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Strong acids/bases dissociate completely in water (indicated by single arrow ->); weak acids/bases dissociate only partially, establishing dynamic equilibrium (indicated by double arrow <=>).
technical_core.why_required: Distinguishes concentration from acid strength.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating acetic acid dissociation as 100% complete.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Neutralization of a strong acid by a strong base is fundamentally the combination of H+(aq) and OH-(aq) to form liquid water, with spectator ions remaining dissolved.
technical_core.why_required: Reveals the true sub-microscopic chemical transformation behind acid-base reactions.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Viewing neutralization as a mysterious disappearance of acid rather than water formation.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: H+ aqueous hydronium/hydrogen ion, OH- aqueous hydroxide ion, H2O neutral liquid water
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Net ionic neutralization
mandatory_equations.conditions_of_validity: Dilute aqueous solution at 25 deg C

representations.name: Hydronium Ion Solvation Model
representations.chemistry_encoded: Water molecule dipole orienting toward proton to form H3O+ ion in aqueous medium
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit water molecule participation in proton hydration
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing bare naked unhydrated protons floating in water
representations.verification_method: Check charge conservation across H+ + H2O -> H3O+

model_conditions.condition: Aqueous solution at 25 deg C
model_conditions.why_needed: Water auto-ionization Kw = [H+][OH-] = 1.0 x 10^-14 holds
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Neutral pH shifts from 7.0 at non-standard temperatures

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify acid/base species and presence of aqueous water solvent
Determine degree of ionization (complete -> vs partial <=>)
Write molecular equation, complete ionic equation, and cancel spectator ions for net ionic equation

required_transformations.description: HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) -> NaCl(aq) + H2O(l) transformed to H+(aq) + OH-(aq) -> H2O(l)
Dry HCl gas does not turn dry litmus paper red because H+ ions are generated only in presence of water

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Substances like dry HCl gas or solid citric acid crystals are acidic by themselves without water
misconceptions.why_plausible: They are named 'acids' on the reagent bottle
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Dry HCl gas passed over dry blue litmus paper shows zero color change; adding one drop of water instantly turns it red
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce: acidic behavior is a property of hydrated H+(aq) / H3O+ ions formed upon aqueous dissolution

mandatory_verifications: SPECTATOR_ION_CANCELLATION_CHECK
CHARGE_BALANCE_NET_IONIC_CHECK

problem_families.recognition_cues: Reaction between acid and base forming salt and water
problem_families.first_technical_move: Split strong electrolytes into dissociated ions and identify non-participating spectator ions
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Splitting water or weak acids into separate free ions in complete ionic equation
problem_families.typical_unknown: Spectator ions and net ionic equation

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Ionization equilibrium distinctions and net ionic spectator cancellations

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Omitting the necessity of water for acid ionization
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Acidity requires aqueous dissociation into hydronium ions

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Redox Reactions, Oxidation States & Electron Transfer

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 10 Science
provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 1, Section 1.2.5 (Oxidation and Reduction)

technical_core.canonical_statement: Oxidation is the loss of electrons (increase in oxidation number); reduction is the gain of electrons (decrease in oxidation number); they occur simultaneously.
technical_core.why_required: Standard universal electron-transfer definition of redox.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Restricting redox solely to oxygen gain/loss.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Oxidation states are assigned by formal rules: free elements are 0, monoatomic ions equal their charge, oxygen is -2 (except peroxides), hydrogen is +1 (with nonmetals), and the sum equals the overall species charge.
technical_core.why_required: Enforces rigorous bookkeeping of electron transfer.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Arbitrary assignment of oxidation numbers.

technical_core.canonical_statement: The oxidizing agent is the reactant species that causes oxidation by accepting electrons (and is itself reduced); the reducing agent donates electrons (and is itself oxidized).
technical_core.why_required: Agent role terminology is systematically inverted relative to the substance oxidized/reduced.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Claiming the substance oxidized is the oxidizing agent.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: CuO copper(II) oxide (Cu reduced from +2 to 0, oxidizing agent), H2 hydrogen gas (H oxidized from 0 to +1, reducing agent)
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Simultaneous electron loss and gain

representations.name: Redox Oxidation Number Tracking Arc Diagram
representations.chemistry_encoded: Balanced equation with oxidation numbers written above elements, connected by bridging arcs labeled 'Oxidation (loss of e-)' and 'Reduction (gain of e-)'
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit numerical tracking of electron gain and loss confirming equal exchange
representations.common_incorrect_version: Drawing arrows without specifying electron transfer numbers
representations.verification_method: Check total electrons lost by reducing agent equals total electrons gained by oxidizing agent

model_conditions.condition: Conservation of charge and electrons
model_conditions.why_needed: Free electrons cannot accumulate in bulk chemical media
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Unbalanced half-reactions violate charge conservation

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Assign oxidation numbers to every atom on reactant and product sides
Identify species whose oxidation number increased (oxidized) and decreased (reduced)
Apply agent inversion rule to designate oxidizing and reducing agents
Verify electron loss equals electron gain across balanced half-reactions

required_transformations.description: Zn + CuSO4 -> ZnSO4 + Cu -> Zn is oxidized (reducing agent), Cu^2+ is reduced (oxidizing agent)
Combine Fe^2+ -> Fe^3+ + e- and MnO4^- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn^2+ + 4H2O by multiplying by 5

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: The oxidizing agent is the substance that gets oxidized
misconceptions.why_plausible: Confusing the agent causing the action with the recipient of the action
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A travel agent sends others on travel; an oxidizing agent oxidizes another substance by taking its electrons, and is therefore reduced itself
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce: Oxidizing agent = species reduced (electron acceptor); Reducing agent = species oxidized (electron donor)

mandatory_verifications: ELECTRON_CONSERVATION_EXCHANGE_CHECK
OXIDATION_NUMBER_SUM_CHECK

problem_families.name: Redox Identification and Agent Assignment
problem_families.recognition_cues: Chemical equation with potential change in oxidation numbers or electron transfer
problem_families.first_technical_move: Assign oxidation states to all atoms before and after arrow
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Classifying the substance oxidized as the oxidizing agent
problem_families.typical_unknown: Substance oxidized, substance reduced, oxidizing agent, reducing agent

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Complex simultaneous electron bookkeeping and linguistic role inversion

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Conflating oxidizing agent with oxidized species
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Oxidizing agent causes oxidation and is itself reduced

subtopic_gates.learner_title: States of Matter: Solid, Liquid, Gas & Kinetic Particle Theory

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: Matter is composed of discrete particles in continuous motion; kinetic energy increases with temperature; intermolecular forces determine physical state.
technical_core.why_required: Microscopic explanation of macroscopic states and compressibility.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Belief that matter is a continuous continuum without particle gaps.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Average kinetic energy of particles proportional to absolute temperature
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Temperature must be strictly in Kelvin

representations.name: Microscopic Solid, Liquid and Gas Particle Arrangement
representations.chemistry_encoded: Three side-by-side boxes showing tightly packed orderly lattice for solid, loosely touching disordered particles for liquid, and widely separated fast particles for gas
mandatory_labels: Gas: Large Mean Free Path, High Speed
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Clear representation of interparticle spacing across phases
representations.common_incorrect_version: Drawing gas particles packed together like liquids
representations.verification_method: Verify density and compressibility hierarchy solid > liquid >> gas

model_conditions.condition: Thermal kinetic energy vs intermolecular attractive potential determines phase.
model_conditions.why_needed: At high pressure and low temperature, all real substances condense.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Gas laws break down under liquefaction conditions.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify macroscopic properties: shape, volume, compressibility.
Relate macroscopic behavior to particle spacing and kinetic energy.

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Believing individual particles expand when a gas expands.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Projecting macroscopic volume expansion onto microscopic particle size.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Gas expansion increases distance between particles; individual atom/molecule radius remains fixed.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Gas volume changes through interparticle spacing, never by swelling of individual atoms.

mandatory_verifications: Verify stoichiometry, mass conservation, and charge balance for CHEM-MATTER-STATES.

problem_families.name: Classification and Particle Modeling of States
problem_families.recognition_cues: Identify state of matter from physical characteristics and kinetic properties
problem_families.first_technical_move: Compare thermal energy with intermolecular attraction
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Assuming solid particles are completely stationary at room temperature

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Kinetic theory of matter and phase properties.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Claiming individual molecules expand when a gas is heated.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Individual molecular dimensions do not expand; only intermolecular distances increase.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Latent Heat of Fusion/Vaporization & Evaporative Cooling

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: During a phase change, heat absorbed (latent heat) overcomes intermolecular bonds without raising temperature; evaporation is a surface phenomenon occurring below boiling point causing cooling.
technical_core.why_required: Explains isothermal phase changes and evaporative thermodynamics.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Belief that temperature continuously rises while ice melts or water boils.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Latent heat equation during phase transition

symbols.name: Specific Latent Heat
symbols.dimension: Latent heat of fusion or vaporization

mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Temperature T remains strictly constant during phase change

representations.name: Isothermal Plateau Heating Curve of Water
representations.chemistry_encoded: Temperature vs heat plot showing horizontal temperature plateaus during melting (0 C) and boiling (100 C)
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Horizontal isothermal plateau where temperature does not change
representations.common_incorrect_version: Drawing continuous upward line with no plateaus during phase change
representations.verification_method: Verify temperature remains flat during melting and vaporization

model_conditions.condition: Phase transition of pure substance occurs at constant temperature under constant pressure.
model_conditions.why_needed: Impurities broaden melting/boiling ranges.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Latent heat strictly accounts for potential energy bond-breaking.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify whether heat changes temperature (Q = m c Delta T) or phase (Q = m L).
On heating curve, identify plateaus where temperature remains constant.

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Believing water gets hotter than 100 C while boiling vigorously at standard atmospheric pressure.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Assuming more vigorous heating forces temperature higher during boiling.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Excess heat merely accelerates liquid-to-vapor phase transition rate (latent heat of vaporization); temperature stays pinned at 100 C.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Temperature of boiling water remains exactly 100 C at 1 atm regardless of burner flame intensity.

mandatory_verifications: Verify stoichiometry, mass conservation, and charge balance for CHEM-MATTER-LATENT-HEAT.

problem_families.name: Heat Required for Multi-phase Temperature Transition
problem_families.recognition_cues: Calculate total heat to convert -10 C ice to 100 C steam
problem_families.first_technical_move: Sum sensible heat stages Q = mc Delta T and latent heat plateaus Q = mL
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Using specific heat formula during isothermal phase transition

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Thermodynamic phase transitions and latent heat.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Asserting that water temperature rises while boiling at standard pressure.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Temperature remains strictly constant during phase transition at 1 atm.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Mixtures: True Solutions, Colloids, Suspensions & Tyndall Effect

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: True solutions (particle < 1 nm, homogeneous, no Tyndall effect); Colloids (1-1000 nm, heterogeneous, exhibit Tyndall light scattering); Suspensions (> 1000 nm, settle on standing).
technical_core.why_required: Phase boundary discrimination and light scattering in dispersed systems.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Belief that all clear-looking mixtures are true molecular solutions.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Mass percentage concentration formula
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Mass of solution must strictly equal Mass of Solute + Mass of Solvent

representations.name: Tyndall Light Scattering in Colloid vs True Solution
representations.chemistry_encoded: Flashlight beam passing invisibly through true solution (no scattering) but forming a visible illuminated beam path through colloid
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Visible illuminated conical path in colloid and invisible path in true solution
representations.common_incorrect_version: Drawing light beam scattered by true salt solution
representations.verification_method: Verify particle size determines optical scattering

model_conditions.condition: Solution mass must be the sum of solute mass and solvent mass.
model_conditions.why_needed: Volumes are not additive due to interstitial packing.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Colloids do not settle under gravity but can be separated by centrifugation.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Calculate total solution mass = solute mass + solvent mass.
Evaluate mass percentage concentration = (solute / solution) * 100.

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Using mass of solvent in the denominator of mass percentage concentration.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Confusing solvent with total solution.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: In 20g salt dissolved in 80g water, solution mass is 100g (20%), not 80g (25%).
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: The denominator is strictly the total mass of solution (solute + solvent).

mandatory_verifications: Verify stoichiometry, mass conservation, and charge balance for CHEM-MIXTURE-SEPARATION.

problem_families.name: Mass and Volume Percentage Concentration Calculations
problem_families.recognition_cues: Find mass percentage of salt in aqueous solution
problem_families.first_technical_move: Calculate total mass of solution and apply (mass solute / mass solution) * 100
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Dividing solute mass by solvent mass instead of solution mass

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Colloidal dispersion and concentration mathematics.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Using solvent mass alone as the denominator in solution concentration.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Denominator must be total solution mass (solute plus solvent).

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Atomic Models: Rutherford Nuclear Planetary Model & Bohr Quantized Shells

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: Rutherford established tiny dense positive nucleus via alpha scattering (most space empty); Bohr resolved orbital electromagnetic radiation collapse by postulating quantized discrete non-radiating energy shells (K, L, M, N).
technical_core.why_required: Foundational structural physics of nuclear and atomic quantization.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Belief that electrons orbit at arbitrary continuous distances from the nucleus.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Bohr Angular Momentum Quantization Condition
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Valid for single-electron hydrogenic systems (H, He+, Li2+)

representations.name: Bohr Quantized Concentric Shell Planetary Model
representations.chemistry_encoded: Central positive nucleus containing protons/neutrons surrounded by discrete concentric circular orbits labelled K (n=1), L (n=2), M (n=3)
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Distinct concentric non-overlapping quantized orbits
representations.common_incorrect_version: Drawing electrons spiraling into nucleus
representations.verification_method: Verify 2n^2 maximum electron capacity per shell

model_conditions.condition: Applies rigorously to single-electron species (H, He+, Li2+).
model_conditions.why_needed: Multi-electron atoms experience electron-electron repulsion and orbital subshell splitting.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Bohr model fails for fine structure and multi-electron spectra.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Recall maximum capacity of nth shell is 2*n^2 (K=2, L=8, M=18, N=32).
Fill shells sequentially from lowest energy inward.

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Believing classical electromagnetic theory allows stable Rutherford planetary electrons.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Ignoring classical Larmor radiation from accelerated charged particles.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Accelerated charge radiates electromagnetic energy continuously, causing orbit to decay in ~10^-11 s.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Bohr postulated non-radiating stationary states to resolve classical electrodynamic collapse.

mandatory_verifications: Verify stoichiometry, mass conservation, and charge balance for CHEM-ATOM-RUTHERFORD-BOHR.

problem_families.name: Bohr-Bury Shell Capacity and Electronic Arrangement
problem_families.recognition_cues: Determine electronic configuration and maximum shell population for elements Z=1 to 20
problem_families.first_technical_move: Apply 2n^2 rule and octet constraint on valence shell
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Placing more than 8 electrons in valence shell

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Historical atomic models and quantized shell structure.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Placing more than 8 electrons in the outermost valence shell for Z <= 20.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Outermost valence shell cannot accommodate more than 8 electrons regardless of 2n^2 capacity.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Valency, Electronic Configuration, Isotopes & Isobars

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: Valency is the combining capacity governed by valence electrons (e- <= 4: valency = e-; e- > 4: valency = 8 - e-); Isotopes share same Z but different A (same chemical, different nuclear); Isobars share same A but different Z.
technical_core.why_required: Nuclear composition discrimination and periodic chemical valence determination.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Belief that isotopes of an element have different chemical reactions.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Average relative atomic mass from isotopic abundances
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Sum of fractional abundances must strictly equal 1.0 (or 100%)

representations.name: Isotope vs Isobar Nuclear Subatomic Inventory Table
representations.chemistry_encoded: Tabular comparison of Cl-35 vs Cl-37 (isotopes: same protons Z=17, different neutrons 18 vs 20) and Ar-40 vs Ca-40 (isobars: same mass number A=40, different Z)
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Clear demonstration that isotopes share identical proton number Z
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing isotopes with different proton numbers
representations.verification_method: Verify A = Z + N for every nuclide

model_conditions.condition: Chemical properties depend exclusively on valence electrons and atomic number Z.
model_conditions.why_needed: Nuclear stability and radioactive decay depend on neutron-proton ratio N/Z.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Mass spectrometry measures abundance-weighted average isotopic mass.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Calculate neutron count N = A - Z.
Compute weighted average atomic mass: A_bar = f1*A1 + f2*A2.

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Believing isotopes of chlorine (Cl-35 and Cl-37) form different chemical compounds with sodium.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Conflating nuclear mass with chemical electronic valence.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Both isotopes have 17 protons and identical 2,8,7 electron configurations; both form identical NaCl.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Chemical reactivity is determined entirely by electron configuration, which is identical for isotopes.

mandatory_verifications: Verify stoichiometry, mass conservation, and charge balance for CHEM-ATOM-ISOTOPES-ISOBARS.

problem_families.name: Average Atomic Mass from Isotope Percentages
problem_families.recognition_cues: Calculate fractional atomic mass of Chlorine from 75% Cl-35 and 25% Cl-37
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Dividing simple unweighted average (35 + 37)/2

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Isotopic composition and fractional atomic weight.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Assigning different proton numbers Z to isotopes of the same element.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Isotopes of the same element must have identical atomic number Z.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Types of Reactions: Combination, Thermal/Electrolytic Decomposition & Displacement

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: Combination (A + B -> AB); Decomposition requires energy input (thermal, electrolytic, photochemical: AB -> A + B); Single Displacement (A + BC -> AC + B governed by reactivity series); Double Displacement (AB + CD -> AD + CB involving ion exchange).
technical_core.why_required: Taxonomy and thermodynamic driving forces of chemical transformations.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Classifying neutralization or double displacement as redox reactions.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Stoichiometric 2:1 volume ratio decomposition of water
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Current applied with trace acid/electrolyte

representations.name: Particulate Interaction Models of Reaction Classes
representations.chemistry_encoded: Four schematic diagrams showing: two reactant molecules fusing into one (combination), one molecule splitting under heat/photons (decomposition), more active element kicking out metal ion (displacement), and two ionic solutions forming insoluble solid precipitate (double displacement)
mandatory_labels: Displacement: Active Metal A Displacing B
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Correct stoichiometric particle counts before and after reaction
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing single displacement with a less reactive metal kicking out a more reactive metal
representations.verification_method: Verify conservation of atoms across all 4 reaction types

model_conditions.condition: Single displacement occurs only if free metal is higher than bonded cation in reactivity series.
model_conditions.why_needed: Precipitation occurs only if product ion concentration product exceeds solubility.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Thermal decomposition requires endothermic enthalpy input.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Examine reactants and products: count species to classify reaction archetype.
Check reactivity series for single displacement spontaneity.

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Believing precipitation and neutralization double displacement reactions are redox processes.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Assuming all chemical reactions involve electron transfer.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: In AgNO3 + NaCl -> AgCl(s) + NaNO3, oxidation numbers of all ions remain unchanged (Ag+1, Na+1, N+5, O-2, Cl-1).
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Double displacement involves mutual ion exchange without transfer of electrons; it is non-redox.

mandatory_verifications: Verify stoichiometry, mass conservation, and charge balance for CHEM-RXN-TYPES-DECOMPOSITION.

problem_families.name: Reaction Classification and Spontaneity Prediction
problem_families.recognition_cues: Classify reaction and predict if Fe + CuSO4 or Cu + FeSO4 occurs
problem_families.first_technical_move: Locate Fe and Cu on reactivity series: Fe is more reactive than Cu
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Predicting reaction occurs when less reactive metal is added to more reactive metal salt

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Reaction taxonomy and displacement thermodynamics.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Predicting displacement of more reactive metal by a less reactive metal (e.g. Cu displacing Fe).
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: A metal can only displace metals located strictly below it in the reactivity series.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: pH Scale, Universal Indicators & Auto-Ionization of Water

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: pH = -log10[H3O+]; pOH = -log10[OH-]; at 25 C, Kw = [H+][OH-] = 10^-14 so pH + pOH = 14; each unit pH change corresponds to 10-fold change in hydronium concentration.
technical_core.why_required: Quantifies aqueous acidity and alkalinity logarithmically.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Belief that a pH change from 6 to 3 means acidity doubled.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Definition of pH and water dissociation constant relation
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Kw = 10^-14 strictly at 25 C (298 K); Kw increases with temperature

representations.name: Universal Indicator Color Spectrum and pH Axis
representations.chemistry_encoded: Color continuum from red (pH 1-3, strong acid) through orange/yellow (pH 4-6) to green (pH 7, neutral) to blue/violet (pH 8-14, alkaline) with marked [H+] logarithmic powers
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Logarithmic 10-fold hydronium factor between integer pH steps
representations.common_incorrect_version: Linear spacing of hydronium concentration on pH axis
representations.verification_method: Verify pH + pOH == 14 at 25 C

model_conditions.condition: Kw = 1.0 x 10^-14 applies strictly at 25 C.
model_conditions.why_needed: Auto-ionization is endothermic: at higher temperature, Kw increases and neutral pH is less than 7.
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Extreme concentrated acids ([H+] > 1 M) can have negative pH.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Convert [H+] to pH via -log10[H+].
For basic solution, compute pOH = -log10[OH-] then pH = 14 - pOH.

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Believing a solution of pH 2 is twice as acidic as pH 4.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Overlooking the logarithmic base-10 definition of pH.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: pH 2 means [H+] = 10^-2 = 0.01 M; pH 4 means [H+] = 10^-4 = 0.0001 M; pH 2 is 100 times more acidic, not twice.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Each step down of 1 pH unit represents a 10-fold increase in hydronium ion concentration.

mandatory_verifications: Verify stoichiometry, mass conservation, and charge balance for CHEM-ACID-PH-INDICATORS.

problem_families.name: Hydronium Concentration and pH from Strong Acids/Bases
problem_families.recognition_cues: Calculate pH of 0.001 M HCl and 0.01 M NaOH at 25 C
problem_families.first_technical_move: For HCl: -log(10^-3) = 3; For NaOH: pOH = -log(10^-2) = 2 -> pH = 12
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Setting pH = 2 for 0.01 M NaOH by confusing [OH-] with [H+]

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Logarithmic acidity scale and aqueous equilibrium.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Treating a difference of 2 pH units as a 2-fold change in acid concentration.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: A difference of 2 pH units strictly represents a 100-fold (10^2) change in [H+].

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Salts: Chlor-Alkali Process, Bleaching Powder, Baking/Washing Soda & POP

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: Chlor-alkali electrolysis of brine produces NaOH, Cl2 (anode), H2 (cathode); Bleaching powder Ca(OCl)Cl from dry slaked lime and Cl2; Baking soda NaHCO3 decomposes on heating to Na2CO3; Plaster of Paris CaSO4.1/2H2O from gypsum CaSO4.2H2O at 373 K.
technical_core.why_required: Industrial preparative inorganic chemistry and domestic chemical salt utilities.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Overheating gypsum above 373 K yields dead burnt plaster (CaSO4) which will not set with water.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Chlor-alkali electrolysis of brine
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Requires membrane or diaphragm cell to keep Cl2 from reacting with NaOH

representations.name: Chlor-Alkali Membrane Electrolytic Cell Schematic
representations.chemistry_encoded: Electrolytic cell with brine inlet, cation-permeable membrane, titanium anode producing Cl2 gas, and steel cathode producing H2 gas and NaOH
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Correct electrode product assignment (Cl2 at anode, H2 and NaOH at cathode)

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Carbon: Tetravalency, Catenation, Allotropes & Covalent Bond Sharing

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.why_required: Explains unique diversity of millions of stable organic compounds.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Belief that graphite cannot conduct electricity because it is a non-metal covalent substance.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Covalent octet completion in methane via electron sharing
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Each C-H shared pair counts as 2 electrons to both atoms

model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Catenation strength stems from exceptionally strong C-C single bond energy (348 kJ/mol).

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Write Lewis dot representation of carbon with 4 valence dots.
Pair each carbon electron with another atom to complete octet.

misconceptions.why_plausible: Assuming all allotropes of non-metals are electrical insulators.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: In graphite, each carbon is bonded to only 3 others in planar hexagonal sheets; the 4th valence electron is delocalized across the sheet, enabling high conductivity.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Graphite is an excellent electrical conductor along its planar graphene sheets due to delocalized mobile pi electrons.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: de Broglie Wavelength & Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: Every moving matter particle exhibits wave nature with de Broglie wavelength lambda = h / p = h / (m v); Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle Delta x * Delta p >= h / (4 pi) establishes that simultaneous exact measurement of position and momentum is physically impossible, invalidating defined Bohr orbits.
technical_core.why_required: Demolishes classical deterministic planetary orbits; necessitates quantum orbital probabilities.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Believing macroscopic moving objects (like a cricket ball) have observable diffraction waves.

mandatory_equations.formula: \lambda = \frac{h}{m v} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m \, \text{KE}}}, \quad \Delta x \cdot \Delta p \ge \frac{h}{4\pi} \implies \Delta x \cdot \Delta v \ge \frac{h}{4\pi m}
mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: de Broglie wavelength and Heisenberg uncertainty equations
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Valid for any mass m; observable wave nature restricted to subatomic particles

representations.name: Localized Wave Packet and Position-Momentum Trade-off
representations.chemistry_encoded: Spatial wave packet showing inverse relationship: tight spatial confinement (small Delta x) produces spread of Fourier wavelengths (large Delta p)
mandatory_labels: Momentum Spread Delta p = h / Delta lambda
Limit Delta x * Delta p >= h / (4 pi)
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Complementary trade-off: narrowing Delta x broadens Delta p
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing simultaneous zero uncertainty Delta x = 0 and Delta p = 0
representations.verification_method: Verify Heisenberg product meets or exceeds h / (4 pi)

model_conditions.condition: Macroscopic objects have negligible de Broglie wavelengths (< 10^-34 m), rendering wave behavior undetectable.
model_conditions.why_needed: Electrons have tiny mass, producing significant de Broglie wavelengths comparable to atomic spacings (~10^-10 m).
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Heisenberg principle fundamentally forbids classical trajectories where position and velocity are simultaneously known.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Calculate de Broglie wavelength lambda = h / (m*v).
Apply Heisenberg relation: Delta x >= h / (4 * pi * m * Delta v).

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Believing electrons travel along well-defined circular railway tracks (orbits) around the nucleus.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Holding onto classical macroscopic planetary models.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: By Heisenberg uncertainty, exact position and momentum cannot be known simultaneously; circular orbits cannot exist.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Electrons do not travel in defined orbits; they occupy 3D probabilistic clouds called orbitals.

mandatory_verifications: Verify stoichiometry, mass conservation, and charge balance for CHEM-ATOM-DE-BROGLIE-UNCERTAINTY.

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Wave-particle duality and fundamental quantum limits.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Claiming both position and velocity of an electron can be measured simultaneously with zero error.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Heisenberg uncertainty principle strictly requires Delta x * Delta p >= h / (4 pi).

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Quantum Numbers, Orbital Shapes (s, p, d) & Radial/Angular Nodes

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: Four quantum numbers specify electron state: n (principal, shell size/energy), l (azimuthal, orbital shape: s=0, p=1, d=2, f=3), ml (magnetic, orientation: -l to +l), ms (spin: +1/2, -1/2); Orbitals have (n - l - 1) radial nodes and l angular nodes; total nodes = n - 1.
technical_core.why_required: Quantum mechanical state specification and 3D wave function nodal topology.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Believing a 2d or 1p orbital can exist in an atom.

mandatory_equations.formula: \text{Radial Nodes} = n - l - 1, \quad \text{Angular Nodes} = l, \quad \text{Total Nodes} = n - 1
mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Orbital nodal count relationships from wave functions
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: l must be strictly less than n (l in [0, n-1])

representations.name: 3D Boundary Surface Shapes of s, p, and d Orbitals
representations.chemistry_encoded: Spherical 1s/2s orbitals (with 2s showing radial node); dumbbell-shaped 2px, 2py, 2pz orbitals with nodal planes; cloverleaf 3dxy, 3dyz, 3dxz, 3dx2-y2 and doughnut 3dz2 orbitals
mandatory_labels: s orbital: Spherical Symmetry (l=0, no angular node)
p orbitals: Dumbbell with 1 Nodal Plane (l=1)
d orbitals: Cloverleaf / Toroid with 2 Nodal Surfaces (l=2)
Radial Node: Spherical Shell where psi^2 = 0
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Accurate nodal plane orientations for px, py, pz and d orbitals
representations.common_incorrect_version: Drawing s orbital with directional lobes or p orbital as spherical
representations.verification_method: Verify total nodes equals n - 1 for every orbital

model_conditions.condition: Azimuthal quantum number l is strictly bounded: 0 <= l <= n - 1.
model_conditions.why_needed: Magnetic quantum number ml is bounded: -l <= ml <= +l (total 2l + 1 orientations).
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Radial probability density is 4*pi*r^2 * R(r)^2; vanishes at r=0 for all orbitals except s-orbitals.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Determine allowed l values for given n (l = 0, ..., n-1).
Determine allowed ml values for given l (ml = -l, ..., +l).
Calculate radial nodes = n - l - 1 and angular nodes = l.

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Believing 1p, 2d, or 3f orbitals exist.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Ignoring the constraint l < n derived from Legendre polynomials.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: For n=1, l can only be 0 (only 1s exists); for n=2, l can only be 0 or 1 (2s, 2p exist, no 2d).
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: An orbital with subshell l requires n >= l + 1; hence 1p, 2d, and 3f are mathematically impossible.

mandatory_verifications: Verify stoichiometry, mass conservation, and charge balance for CHEM-ATOM-QUANTUM-NUMBERS.

problem_families.name: Validity of Quantum Number Sets and Node Counts

problem_families.common_fatal_error: Allowing l = n or |ml| > l

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Quantum numbers and orbital wave function geometry.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Assigning azimuthal quantum number l equal to principal quantum number n (e.g. 2d orbital with n=2, l=2).
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Azimuthal quantum number l must be strictly less than n (l <= n - 1).

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Electronic Configuration: Aufbau Principle, Pauli Exclusion & Hund's Rule

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: Aufbau (n + l rule: lower n+l fills first; if tied, lower n fills first); Pauli Exclusion Principle (no two electrons in an atom can have the same four quantum numbers; max 2 e- per orbital with opposite spins); Hund's Rule (orbitals of equal energy are singly occupied with parallel spins before pairing); Anomalous stability of half-filled (d5) and fully-filled (d10) subshells (Cr: [Ar] 4s1 3d5, Cu: [Ar] 4s1 3d10).
technical_core.why_required: Ground-state electron configuration determination across the periodic table.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Pairing electrons in degenerate p or d orbitals before each orbital has one electron.

symbols.name: Parallel Spin Electron Count
symbols.dimension: Number of degenerate electrons with same spin

mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: 4s (n+l = 4+0 = 4) fills before 3d (n+l = 3+2 = 5)
mandatory_equations.conditions_of_validity: Neutral isolated multi-electron atoms in ground state

representations.name: Orbital Box Diagrams Demonstrating Aufbau, Pauli, and Hund Rules
representations.chemistry_encoded: Box diagram for Carbon (1s2 2s2 2px1 2py1 with parallel spins), Chromium ([Ar] 4s1 3d5 with 6 parallel spins), and Copper ([Ar] 4s1 3d10)
mandatory_labels: Pauli: Max 2 Electrons with Opposite Spins (Up/Down)
Hund: Maximum Parallel Spins in Degenerate Orbitals
Anomalous Half/Fully Filled d Subshell (Cr, Cu)
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Correct parallel spins in separate degenerate boxes for Hund's rule
representations.common_incorrect_version: Pairing electrons in 2px before putting an electron in 2py
representations.verification_method: Verify total electron count equals atomic number Z

model_conditions.condition: Aufbau order: 1s < 2s < 2p < 3s < 3p < 4s < 3d < 4p < 5s < 4d < 5p < 6s < 4f < 5d.
model_conditions.why_needed: When transition metals ionize, electrons are lost from 4s BEFORE 3d (e.g. Fe: [Ar] 4s2 3d6 -> Fe2+: [Ar] 3d6).

Recognize Cr (Z=24: 4s1 3d5) and Cu (Z=29: 4s1 3d10) exceptions.

misconceptions.why_plausible: Assuming electrons are removed in the reverse order of Aufbau filling.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Once 3d is populated, 4s electrons have higher radial probability further from nucleus; Fe loses 4s electrons first to form Fe2+ ([Ar] 3d6).
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: In transition metal ionization, outermost 4s electrons are strictly removed before inner 3d electrons.

mandatory_verifications: Verify stoichiometry, mass conservation, and charge balance for CHEM-ATOM-ELECTRONIC-CONFIG.

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Aufbau subshell ordering, spin multiplicity, and exchange stability.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Pairing two electrons with anti-parallel spins in one p orbital while degenerate p orbitals remain completely empty.
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Hund's rule requires degenerate orbitals to be occupied singly with parallel spins before pairing occurs.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: VSEPR Theory: Electron Pair Repulsions, Steric Numbers & Molecular Geometries

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: Electron pairs around a central atom repel and adopt spatial geometries that maximize distance; Repulsion hierarchy: Lone Pair - Lone Pair (lp-lp) > Lone Pair - Bond Pair (lp-bp) > Bond Pair - Bond Pair (bp-bp); Steric number SN = (sigma bonds + lone pairs) dictates electron geometry; lone pairs compress bond angles below ideal values (CH4: 109.5, NH3: 107, H2O: 104.5); Equatorials vs axial in trigonal bipyramidal (lone pairs prefer equatorial sites to minimize 90 repulsions).
technical_core.why_required: 3D molecular stereochemistry and bond angle distortions from electron domain repulsion.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Placing lone pairs in axial positions in PCl3F2 or SF4.

mandatory_equations.formula: \text{SN} = \text{Number of } \sigma \text{ Bonds} + \text{Number of Lone Pairs on Central Atom}

representations.chemistry_encoded: 3D ball-and-stick geometries: Linear (SN=2, 180), Trigonal Planar/Bent (SN=3, 120), Tetrahedral/Pyramidal/Bent (SN=4, 109.5), Trigonal Bipyramidal/See-saw/T-shaped/Linear (SN=5), Octahedral/Square Pyramidal/Square Planar (SN=6)
mandatory_labels: SN=6: XeF4 (Square Planar, 2 lp in Axial)
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Correct distinction between electron geometry and molecular shape
representations.common_incorrect_version: Calling NH3 tetrahedral shape instead of trigonal pyramidal

misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Molecular shape is defined by positions of atoms only, while electron geometry includes lone pair domains.

mandatory_verifications: Verify stoichiometry, mass conservation, and charge balance for CHEM-BOND-VSEPR-GEOMETRY.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Valence Bond Theory: Orbital Overlap & Hybridization (sp, sp2, sp3, sp3d, sp3d2)

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: Valence Bond Theory: covalent bond forms by pairing opposite-spin electrons in overlapping atomic orbitals; Sigma bond forms by coaxial head-on overlap (stronger); Pi bond forms by lateral sideways overlap of unhybridized p orbitals (weaker); Hybridization is mathematical mixing of non-equivalent atomic orbitals (s, p, d) on same atom to form degenerate, directed hybrid orbitals matching VSEPR geometries (sp: linear 180, sp2: trigonal planar 120, sp3: tetrahedral 109.5).
technical_core.why_required: Quantum mechanical basis of directional covalent bonding and stereochemistry.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Asserting a pi bond can form without a prior coaxial sigma bond.

misconceptions.required_counterexample: Hybrid orbitals are designed for maximum axial overlap; pi bonds are formed exclusively by sideways overlap of unhybridized pure p or d orbitals.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Hybrid orbitals form strictly sigma bonds; pi bonds are formed solely by unhybridized atomic orbitals.

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Molecular Orbital Theory: LCAO, Bonding/Antibonding MOs, Bond Order & Paramagnetism

provenance.source_curriculum: NCERT Grade 9-11 Chemistry / CBSE Secondary Curriculum

technical_core.canonical_statement: Linear Combination of Atomic Orbitals (LCAO) produces bonding MOs (in-phase constructive interference, lower energy) and antibonding MOs (out-of-phase destructive interference with nodal plane, higher energy); Bond Order = (1/2)(N_b - N_a); Molecule is stable if Bond Order > 0; Explains paramagnetism of O2 (two unpaired electrons in degenerate pi* 2px, pi* 2py antibonding MOs, which Lewis theory fails to explain); MO filling order changes for Z <= 7 (s-p mixing shifts sigma 2pz above pi 2px, pi 2py).
technical_core.why_required: Delocalized molecular electronic structure, bond order, and magnetic moment prediction.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Applying Z > 7 MO energy order (sigma 2pz below pi 2p) to B2, C2, or N2 (Z <= 7).

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Bond Order formula and Spin-Only Magnetic Moment

O2 (16 e-): sigma 2pz (2 e-) below pi 2p (4 e-), BO = (10-6)/2 = 2
O2 Paramagnetism: 2 Unpaired Electrons in pi* 2px and pi* 2py
Antibonding Nodal Plane between Nuclei (sigma* and pi*)

misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Molecular Orbital Theory correctly demonstrates that O2 has 2 unpaired electrons in pi* antibonding MOs and is paramagnetic.
